decision_description: Tier 2B extracted/evaluation_priority_weights.json listed all three MSCA-PF evaluation criteria (Excellence, Impact, Quality and Efficiency of Implementation) as status Assumed with null numeric weights, because Annex D of the Work Programme General Annexes — the formal source of criterion percentage weights — was not in the declared Tier 2B inputs for the call slice. Phase 1 call analysis located the authoritative criterion weights in the MSCA evaluation form ef_he-msca_en.pdf, a Tier 2A instrument schema source, which explicitly states: Excellence 50%, Impact 30%, Quality and Efficiency of Implementation 20%. These confirmed Tier 2A weights are recorded in call_analysis_summary.json evaluation_matrix and govern over the Assumed Tier 2B null values. Conflict: Tier 2B evaluation_priority_weights.json (status Assumed, null weights for all three criteria) versus Tier 2A ef_he-msca_en.pdf (status Confirmed, explicit percentage weights derived from named evaluation form sections). Resolution: Tier 2A governs per CLAUDE.md §3 authority hierarchy (Tier 2A rank 4 supersedes Tier 2B rank 5); Tier 2B Assumed values are not contradicted but are superseded by the higher-authority Confirmed source.
alternatives_considered: Retain Assumed status for all three criteria throughout call_analysis_summary.json and proceed with null weights, flagging evaluation_matrix as unresolved for downstream phases including Phase 8 drafting
Derive criterion weights from MSCA Programme Guide or primary Tier 1 legislation as a higher-priority authority, deferring to Tier 1 rather than Tier 2A
Use the Assumed Tier 2B criterion names only (without numeric weights) in call_analysis_summary.json and defer weight confirmation to the concept refiner agent in Phase 2
Treat the Tier 2B Assumed values as authoritative on the basis that they were the first extracted representation, requiring a formal override record before substitution
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §3 authority hierarchy: Tier 2A instrument schemas (ef_he-msca_en.pdf evaluation form, priority rank 4) governs over Tier 2B topic and call sources (docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/evaluation_priority_weights.json, status Assumed, priority rank 5); when Tier 2A provides a Confirmed value for a field that Tier 2B holds only as Assumed, Tier 2A supersedes per the rank ordering in CLAUDE.md §3 Table
rationale: The MSCA evaluation form ef_he-msca_en.pdf is a Tier 2A instrument schema that explicitly states criterion weights with percentage values in named sections: 'Section 1. Excellence — Score 1 (0-5): Weighting: 50%', 'Section 2. Impact — Score 2 (0-5): Weighting: 30%', 'Section 3. Quality and efficiency of the implementation — Score 3 (0-5): Weighting: 20%'. Per CLAUDE.md §3, Tier 2A (rank 4) is a higher authority than Tier 2B (rank 5). The Tier 2B evaluation_priority_weights.json correctly and honestly flagged the weights as Assumed when its declared source documents did not include Annex D; this was not an error but a correct status assignment under CLAUDE.md §12.2. Once the Tier 2A evaluation form was read during Phase 1 call analysis and provided Confirmed weights, those values supersede the Tier 2B assumptions without contradiction — the Tier 2B file was incomplete, not wrong. Recording the confirmed weights in call_analysis_summary.json evaluation_matrix is constitutionally required (CLAUDE.md §9.4, §12.2) and directly implements the gate_02 population requirement. This resolution enables downstream phases to use confirmed evaluation weighting for evaluator-oriented section drafting in Phase 8.
